# 荷莫茲有限通航方案重啟賣壓，Alphabet仍找到買方

## 油價反轉，短端吐回漲幅

擬議荷莫茲安排的細節，不如投資人期待的全面開放，美債因而下跌。伊朗官員表示，與阿曼商議的協議不會提供完整通行權；當地報導更指，美國、以色列及其他被列為敵對國家的船隻可能被排除。WTI上漲3.80%至$78.08。

2年期及5年期殖利率各升7個基點至4.25%、4.40%，10年期升6個基點至4.69%，30年期升5個基點至5.22%。10年期升幅大部分來自損益兩平通膨率增加4個基點至2.26%，實質殖利率另升2個基點至2.43%。本週稍早油價下降對債市的幫助，建立在通航確實恢復的期待上；週四浮現的限制，削弱了這個前提。

聯準會官員保留通膨持續時加大動作的可能，經濟數據卻非全面偏鷹。初領失業金僅199,000人，企業宣布裁員也減少；續領人數上升，則顯示重新找到工作可能更難。生產力優於預期、單位勞動成本低於預期，也提供了產出保持韌性而成本壓力減輕的可能。

信用買方同時承接Alphabet的$250億發行，最高訂單約$1,150億。在公債下跌時完成如此規模融資，確實顯示市場容量，但讓利有助吸引需求，Alphabet舊券也仍承壓。折現率上升尚未關閉資本市場，卻使每筆交易的價格與結構更重要。

## 勞動市場有韌性，生產力也改善

2年期及5年期跌幅最大，反映能源通膨再起最直接影響這些年期的政策預期。曲線小幅趨平，2s10s收窄1個基點至44，2s30s收窄2個基點至97。2年期不只吐回週三跌幅；長債當日升幅雖較小，30年期近一個月仍高23個基點，2年期則高12個基點。

抗通膨債把當日催化因素與較長期變化區分開來。10年期損益兩平通膨率升4個基點至2.26%，實質殖利率升2個基點至2.43%。但近一個月名目殖利率上升21個基點，其中19個基點來自實質殖利率，通膨補償僅2個基點。週四能源反轉對通膨補償的影響，明顯大於整月走勢所呈現的程度。

伊朗—阿曼安排據稱已進入最後階段，但伊朗官員強調，這不是全面重開海峽，美國也不是協議一方。敵對國家船隻可能受限的報導，更使航運正常化前景複雜。油價盤中一度漲逾5%，WTI最終收高3.80%。外交協議與不受限制的通行之間，仍有一段距離，而這個落差又直接進入債券定價。

美國勞動數據未顯示突然大量解僱。初領失業金199,000人，低於預估202,000人，接近修正後前值198,000人。Challenger公布7月企業宣布裁員由45,849人降至33,429人，遠低於預估59,000人。但續領失業金由修正後177.7萬人升至180.1萬人，高於預估179萬人。新裁員少與再就業變慢可以同時發生，不能只靠單一數列判斷整體勞動市場。

第2季非農生產力初值增加1.4%，為預估0.6%的兩倍以上，也高於修正後前值0.8%。單位勞動成本增加1.3%，與修正後前值相同，低於預估2.1%。每名勞工產出提高，可在需求維持時控制成本。6月批發庫存增加0.2%，預估0.3%。這些數據緩和了經濟韌性的通膨含義，但生產力改善能否持續仍待觀察。

今年沒有投票權、支持7月維持利率的Mary Daly，仍認為暫時性通膨較可能。關稅、能源與AI相關壓力可能消退，使利率不必調整；但她對另一種情境的態度更強硬：若衝擊相互累積、形成持續通膨，就不一定只應漸進緊縮，而可能需要快速行動。她也警告，長期預期在2022年後已上升，若再走高將更難扭轉。

另一位無投票權官員Alberto Musalem在7月支持升息25個基點，並反對以未來可能的生產力紅利，換取容忍當前通膨。他看到關稅影響消退、油價下跌的良性路徑，也看到通膨停在2.5%至3%甚至更高的持續情境。對他而言，月增率略低於0.2%，才是朝2%目標前進的實際證據；若通膨持續，就需要稍高利率。

主席Kevin Warsh據報願意在後續通膨數據偏熱時於9月升息，同時維持有限的前瞻指引。9月升息定價已由他前次記者會前約70%，降至60%以下。非農及下週通膨數據前，1天期美元選擇權成本升至7月30日以來最高，1週期波動率也上升。缺乏數據如何對應決策的明確指引，使每次公布更可能改變市場對行動日期的判斷。

川普不時致電Warsh詢問預測及意見的報導，也使兩者關係受到檢視，但沒有跡象顯示通話談到利率。這個區別重要：市場面對的是政策架構與溝通的不確定性，而非某次利率決策受行政部門指示的證據。Warsh願意依賴市場殖利率上升來抑制需求，仍是投資人決定長債需要多少補償時的一項考量。

## Alphabet巨額發行完成，舊券承受供給壓力

LQD下跌0.36%，HYG及JNK僅跌0.08%、0.06%。長天期AAA至A及BBB企業債指數各跌0.71%、0.63%，20年以上美債指數跌0.59%。較大的市值損失集中在存續期間，而非投機級基金同步大幅走弱。

Alphabet發行$250億，分成10個券別、年期由2年至40年。最高訂單約$1,150億，在報導列舉的AI交易中，僅次於Oracle約$1,290億及Amazon約$1,260億。40年期以美債加130個基點定價，初步討論約155個基點。投資人可以選擇廣泛年期，較慷慨的初始溢價也有助累積訂單。

這筆交易使Alphabet自2025年初以來發行超過$1,140億，其中2026上半年跨幣別籌資已逾$500億。公司告訴投資人，打算每年兩次在美國發債；支出預測升至最多$2,050億，資本支出也促成2004年IPO以來首次季度現金流轉負。2月$200億發行的債券，週四利差高於當時發行水準。新資金取得能力仍強，但既有持有人已承擔部分持續供給成本。

本週美國投資級發行達$800億，為今年第三高。Alphabet自初步討論收窄利差，部分來自起始價格具吸引力，不代表如此規模能毫不費力地按既有次級市場價格成交。新券與2月舊券後續如何交易，比最高訂單更能顯示需求能否持續。

資料中心證券化的接受度較吃力。最近三筆CMBS中有兩筆，包括CyrusOne及QTS Realty Trust擔保的交易，都須比初步討論擴大利差才找到買方。截至7月28日，資料中心CMBS發行約$57億，占全部CMBS的7.3%。AAA單一借款人資料中心利差為SOFR加168個基點，一年前153；BBB-為332個基點，一年前321。

QTS最新交易20年到期，10年後可提前償還，讓借款人在技術淘汰風險更高前有再融資機會，也要求投資人同時評估提前收回與繼續曝險。較小的Blue Owl交易，以維吉尼亞州一座出租予投資級大型雲端業者的資料中心為擔保，則按初步討論定價。同產業內，租戶品質、槓桿與規模仍使結果不同。

United Wholesale Mortgage需要資本的原因不同。這家美國最大房貸業者公布淨損$4.52億、暫停股利，並宣布Oaktree Capital Management及執行長Mat Ishbia家族持有的投資工具，合計注資$20.5億。方案包括立即$16.5億及計畫中的$4億現金增資。與收購Two Harbors失敗相關的利率避險損失達$6.03億，是季度損失的重要來源。

Oaktree要求的保障遠超過高收益。特別股初期基本股利至少10%，即每年$1.5億，未以現金支付的部分加入本金；贖回溢價隨時間可升至60%。若7年後Oaktree仍持有至少25%特別股，就可取得董事會多數並推動清算。認股權全數行使，可能代表UWM約18%股權。融資增加流動性，但把複利累積的請求權及可能決定性的控制權，放在普通股之前。

日本企業債市場則透過較傳統的保障擴大。1至7月附財務或契約保障條款的發行達JPY468億，超過2025全年JPY446億，更多BBB借款人改用債券而非完全依靠銀行。近期發行人包括BBB+的Gree Holdings及Ichigo，Furukawa也準備類似交易。控制權變更條款允許在收購提高槓桿、導致下市或降評時提前還款。發行人基礎擴大，同時伴隨更強債權保障。

## 日本標售過關，需求卻集中

日本30年期標售緩和超長債失序下跌的疑慮，但結果有好有壞。投標倍數3.86，高於12個月平均3.49，低於7月4.55；尾差擴大，單一大型買方取得24%。即使如此，標售後30年期殖利率降6.5個基點至3.895%，20年期降5個基點至3.64%。接近4%確實吸引買方，但集中度及相對7月表現，仍限制了對需求強度的解讀。

市場給予9月日本銀行升息約62%的機率，IMF的Dan Katz表示，通膨略高於目標，仍有持續正常化空間。首相高市早苗的成長、國防措施及擬議兩年食品稅減免，也留下財政疑問。標售較平穩可減少對美債的眼前外溢，但更高本地殖利率仍可能讓日本儲蓄留在國內。

聯準會最新揭露，對日圓干預的一項資金路徑給了具體答案。截至8月5日一週，FIMA平均使用為零，已連續8週未用，因此揭露期間近期操作並未透過該機制融資。外國貨幣當局從聯準會外國官方逆附買回池提走約$170億，餘額降至$3,180億，兩週已減近$350億。這顯示官方機構動用現金，卻未指出是哪一個當局提領。

FIMA隔夜成本3.75%，1週期為OIS加25個基點，高於民間附買回；每日每交易對手$600億上限，也接近近期一筆日本干預估計規模。未使用不等於已賣出美債，存款、到期證券及民間融資仍是其他選項。這次揭露縮小了資金來源的不確定範圍，尚未辨認最終動用的準備資產。

墨西哥央行一致維持6.50%，並重申下次會議應保持該利率。改變在通膨預測：回到3%的時間由2027年第2季延至第4季。整體通膨雖降至3.1%，服務通膨仍4.36%；2年期交換利率升5個基點至6.72%，回應的是持續性及指引，而非意外的利率決策。

印度在5.25%維持利率後繼續走向另一邊。1年期交換領跌，預期下次升息由10月移至12月，未來一年計入約50個基點，而非會前約75。印度央行已把截至2027年3月年度成長預測由6.6%升至6.7%，通膨仍在2%至6%區間，盧比也自低點回升近2%。投資人給央行更多時間，確認暫時供給壓力是否擴散至核心通膨。

俄羅斯寬鬆卻面對較差的通膨修正。央行7月降息25個基點至14%，同時把年底通膨由4.5%至5.5%升至6%至7%，2026成長則由0.5%至1.5%降至0%至1%；年度通膨已達6.11%。普丁公開偏好低利率，企業也要求紓解，與戰時財政需求一起增加壓力。央行保留2027年4%目標，使結果更依賴當前衝擊屬暫時性的判斷。

## 哥倫比亞暫停後仍有異議，阿根廷延長準備後盾

油價與美國殖利率上升，新興美元債共同環境轉差。美元指數漲0.26%至99.95，EMB跌0.23%，15年期以上美元主權債指數跌0.14%；後者仍優於美國長存續期間信用債。荷莫茲限制浮現後，南非幣及匈牙利福林等能源進口國貨幣走弱，烏克蘭美元債則在各國中跌幅領先。

哥倫比亞央行理事Mauricio Villamizar表示，12%利率不足以在2027年底前把通膨壓到目標區間上緣4%以下。他在7月31日主張升息50個基點，最終表決4比3維持。預測2026年底通膨近7%，2027仍逾4%，目標則為3%、容忍上下1個百分點。財政擴張及薪資增幅高於生產力，使更多調整責任落在貨幣政策。

失去IMF彈性信用額度後，準備適足指標惡化，央行也計畫透過賣權累積最多$40億準備。披索今年升近20%，並連續第3個交易日上漲，收復準備公告後跌幅。Villamizar將計畫定義為重建緩衝，而非匯率目標。但買美元仍把這項工作，連到先前有助控制進口通膨的匯率強勢。

阿根廷取得更具體的準備緩衝。央行與中國人民銀行續簽約$190億換匯協議5年，流動性來源延續至2027總統選舉之後。阿根廷此前依靠國內美元借款、銀行貸款及多邊保證，而非接受外部債市要求的殖利率；續約讓它有更多時間重建緩衝及處理外幣義務。這是官方流動性增加，不是已完成重返國際債市。

菲律賓投資人早已為持續通膨要求更多殖利率。10年期7月升52個基點至約7.25%，本幣債跌1.74%，為東南亞最弱。7月通膨連續第3個月放緩至6.2%，卻仍遠高於全年3%目標，市場計入8月27日升息25個基點。

分析師預期10年期殖利率介於7.20%至7.60%，其中一項預測達7.60%至7.80%；超過7.50%時，陡峭曲線對進一步升息提供較多補償，需求可望改善。因此，最近通膨放緩仍不足以消除當地存續期間風險，尤其當油價及美元又轉強。

## 能源反轉，股票波動率仍低

WTI漲3.80%至$78.08、美元漲0.26%至99.95，同時美債通膨補償與實質殖利率上升。黃金期貨也漲1.72%至$4,318.80。能源反轉重啟通膨疑慮，卻沒有消除對政策與地緣政治不確定性的保護需求。

股市相對平靜。S&P 500跌0.18%，Nasdaq 100跌0.39%，半導體反而漲0.33%，VIX降4.17%至15.15。即使債券投資人減記存續期間部位、要求AI債更多讓利，也沒有出現全面撤離風險的模式。

初級市場最清楚證明融資仍可取得：Alphabet在公債下跌時完成巨額發行。高收益基金跌幅小於投資級存續期間，新興市場損失也溫和。壓力最明顯在利率與特定交易條件，而非整個市場無法移轉風險。

## 非農，以及Alphabet發行後的交易表現

8月7日非農預估新增80,000人，前值57,000人，失業率維持4.2%。報告將有助區分新解僱仍少，以及續領失業金暗示的再就業困難。招聘廣度、薪資及參與率須與標題數字一起看。招聘強、薪資穩，會使Daly快速回應情境及Musalem通膨疑慮更具意義；就業與成本較弱，則降低再升息的急迫性。

荷莫茲需要對船公司及保險業真正可行的通行，而非部分當事方達成協議。船旗被排除、攻擊或保險障礙持續，都會保留週四的能源風險；若接受的航線上交通增加，運費及保險摩擦降低，就能恢復先前油價帶動債市反彈的實際基礎。

Alphabet次級交易將檢驗訂單是否代表在新價格上的持久容量。投資人可比較新2至40年期曲線、2月債券及後續企業或資料中心交易。舊券穩定、新券接近次級價格成交，代表讓利可能足夠；反覆擴大利差或更高溢價，則顯示持續發行仍對投資級及證券化信用組合造成壓力。
zh-TW.methodology_note: 除非另有說明，市場水準均以紐約收盤為準。

overall_summary.headline: 荷莫茲有限通航方案重啟賣壓，Alphabet仍找到買方
overall_summary.session_narrative:
伊朗警告與阿曼的安排不代表全面重開荷莫茲，WTI上漲3.80%至$78.08。2年期殖利率升7個基點至4.25%，10年期升6個基點至4.69%，其中通膨補償增加4個基點。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
# Restricted Hormuz plan revives the selloff, but Alphabet finds buyers

## Oil reverses and the front end gives back its gains

Treasuries sold off as details of a proposed Hormuz arrangement fell short of the reopening investors had anticipated. WTI rose 3.80% to $78.08 after Iranian officials said the contemplated agreement with Oman would not provide full access. Local reports suggested vessels from the US, Israel and other designated hostile countries could be excluded.

Two- and five-year yields rose 7 basis points to 4.25% and 4.40%, the ten-year rose 6 to 4.69%, and the 30-year gained 5 to 5.22%. Most of the ten-year move came from a 4-basis-point increase in the breakeven to 2.26%; the real yield rose another 2 basis points to 2.43%. The oil decline that had helped bonds earlier in the week had depended on reopening becoming a practical reality. Thursday's restrictions weakened that assumption.

Fed officials left open a stronger response if inflation persisted, but the economic data were not uniformly hawkish. Initial claims remained low at 199,000 and announced layoffs declined, while rising continuing claims suggested a harder search for new work. Productivity grew more than expected and unit labor costs less, offering a way for resilient output to coexist with lower cost pressure.

Credit buyers, meanwhile, absorbed Alphabet's $25 billion sale with about $115 billion of peak orders. That was a substantial financing success during a government-bond selloff, though concessions helped attract demand and older Alphabet bonds remained under pressure. Higher discount rates had not closed capital markets; they were making price and structure more important to each transaction.

## Labor resilience meets better productivity

The selloff was largest at two and five years, where renewed energy inflation can most directly affect expected Fed policy. The curve flattened modestly: 2s10s narrowed 1 basis point to 44 and 2s30s narrowed 2 to 97. The two-year yield more than gave back Wednesday's decline, while the long bond's smaller daily move left it 23 basis points higher over a month, compared with 12 at two years.

The inflation-linked split distinguished the day's catalyst from the longer rise in yields. Ten-year breakevens widened 4 basis points to 2.26%, and real yields rose 2 to 2.43%. Over a month, however, the nominal yield was up 21 basis points, of which 19 came through the real yield and only 2 through breakevens. Thursday's energy reversal changed inflation compensation more sharply than the month-long pattern would suggest.

The Iran-Oman arrangement was described as being in its final stages, but Iranian officials emphasized that it was not a full reopening and that the US was not a party. Reports of restrictions on hostile-country vessels further complicated the prospect of normalized shipping. Oil rose more than 5% intraday before WTI settled 3.80% higher. The gap between a diplomatic agreement and unrestricted traffic was again feeding directly into bond pricing.

US labor data showed little evidence of a sudden wave of dismissals. Initial claims were 199,000, below the 202,000 consensus and close to the revised 198,000 prior reading. Challenger's July announced job cuts fell to 33,429 from 45,849, well below the 59,000 forecast. Continuing claims rose to 1.801 million, however, from a revised 1.777 million and above the 1.790 million estimate. Low new layoffs and slower re-employment can coexist, making the labor picture less straightforward than either series alone.

Preliminary second-quarter nonfarm productivity increased 1.4%, more than twice the 0.6% forecast and above the revised 0.8% prior pace. Unit labor costs rose 1.3%, unchanged from the revised previous reading and below the 2.1% consensus. Stronger output per worker can contain costs even when demand holds up. June wholesale inventories increased 0.2%, against 0.3% expected. The releases tempered the inflation implications of resilient activity without settling whether productivity gains would persist.

Mary Daly, a nonvoter who supported the July hold, still considered temporary inflation the more likely outcome. Tariff, energy and AI-related pressures could fade enough to leave rates unchanged. Her alternative scenario was more forceful: if those shocks compound into persistent inflation, she questioned the need to tighten only incrementally and suggested moving quickly. She also warned that a further rise in long-run expectations would be harder to reverse after their increase since 2022.

Alberto Musalem, another nonvoter who favored a quarter-point increase in July, rejected accepting current inflation in exchange for an anticipated productivity windfall. He saw a benign path if tariff effects faded and oil fell, but also a persistent path with inflation around 2.5%–3% or higher. Monthly readings slightly below 0.2% were his practical test for movement back toward 2%; the persistent case would require somewhat higher rates.

Chairman Kevin Warsh was reported to be open to a September increase if coming inflation data were hot, while intending to retain limited forward guidance. September hike pricing had slipped below 60%, from about 70% before his previous press conference. One-day dollar-option costs rose to their highest since July 30, and one-week volatility increased before payrolls and next week's inflation report. With little guidance on how releases map into decisions, individual data points carried more policy-date risk.

Reports that President Donald Trump periodically called Warsh for forecasts and opinions added scrutiny of the relationship, but there was no indication they discussed rates. That distinction matters. The market concern is uncertainty about the policy framework and communication, not evidence that a particular rate decision was directed by the executive. Warsh's willingness to rely on higher market yields to restrain demand remains part of that debate as investors decide how much compensation they need to hold long bonds.

## Alphabet clears a jumbo sale; older paper feels the weight

LQD fell 0.36%, while HYG and JNK lost only 0.08% and 0.06%. Long-maturity AAA–A and BBB corporate indexes declined 0.71% and 0.63%, compared with 0.59% for Treasuries beyond 20 years. The larger mark-to-market losses were concentrated in duration rather than an equally large move across speculative-grade funds.

Alphabet sold $25 billion across ten tranches ranging from two to 40 years. Peak orders of about $115 billion ranked behind only the cited Oracle and Amazon AI deals, at roughly $129 billion and $126 billion. The 40-year tranche priced 130 basis points over Treasuries, down from initial discussion near 155. Investors could choose across a wide maturity range, and a more generous starting premium helped build the book.

The sale takes Alphabet's issuance since early 2025 above $114 billion, following more than $50 billion across currencies in the first half of 2026. The company told investors it intends to issue US debt twice a year. Its spending forecast has risen to as much as $205 billion, and capital expenditure contributed to its first negative-cash-flow quarter since the 2004 IPO. Bonds from February's $20 billion deal traded wider than their issue levels on Thursday. Access to new money remained strong, but existing holders were already bearing some of the cost of the recurring calendar.

Weekly US investment-grade issuance reached $80 billion, the year's third-highest total. Alphabet's spread tightening from initial discussion was partly a function of the attractive starting point, rather than evidence that such volume cleared effortlessly at existing secondary levels. How the new bonds trade alongside February's paper will offer a better view of lasting demand than the peak orderbook alone.

Data-center securitizations showed a more difficult reception. Two of the last three CMBS transactions, including CyrusOne- and QTS Realty Trust-backed deals, widened from initial discussion to secure buyers. Data-center CMBS issuance totaled about $5.7 billion, or 7.3% of all CMBS through July 28. AAA single-borrower data-center spreads were 168 basis points over SOFR, up from 153 a year earlier; BBB- spreads were 332, up from 321.

QTS's latest deal has a 20-year maturity with an option to repay after ten years. That gives the borrower a refinancing opportunity before technology obsolescence becomes more acute, while requiring investors to assess both early repayment and continued exposure. A smaller Blue Owl deal backed by a Virginia data center leased to an investment-grade hyperscaler priced in line with initial discussion. Tenant quality, leverage and size still differentiated deals within the same sector.

United Wholesale Mortgage needed capital for a different reason. The largest US mortgage lender reported a $452 million net loss, suspended its dividend and announced a $2.05 billion infusion from Oaktree Capital Management and a vehicle owned by Chief Executive Mat Ishbia and his family. The package comprises $1.65 billion immediately and a planned $400 million rights offering. A $603 million loss on rate hedges tied to the failed Two Harbors acquisition contributed to the quarterly damage.

The protection demanded by Oaktree extends well beyond a high yield. Its preferred initially pays a base dividend of at least 10%, or $150 million annually, with unpaid cash added to principal. Redemption premiums can rise to 60%. If Oaktree still holds at least 25% of the preferred after seven years, it can obtain a board majority and pursue liquidation. Fully exercised warrants could represent about 18% of UWM's equity. The financing adds liquidity while putting compounding claims and potentially decisive control rights ahead of common shareholders.

Japan's corporate market was broadening with more conventional safeguards. Covenant-bearing issuance reached JPY46.8 billion in January–July, exceeding the JPY44.6 billion sold in all of 2025, as more BBB borrowers used bonds instead of relying exclusively on banks. Recent issuers included BBB+ rated Gree Holdings and Ichigo, with Furukawa preparing a similar sale. Change-of-control clauses permit early repayment when a takeover increases leverage, causes delisting or produces a downgrade. A wider issuer base is arriving alongside stronger creditor rights.

## Japan's auction passes, with demand concentrated

Japan's 30-year auction eased fears of disorderly super-long selling, though the results were mixed. Bid-to-cover of 3.86 exceeded the 12-month average of 3.49 but fell below July's 4.55. The tail widened, and a single large buyer took 24% of the sale. Even so, the 30-year yield fell 6.5 basis points to 3.895% afterward and the 20-year declined 5 to 3.64%. Yields near 4% attracted buyers, but the concentration and comparison with July qualified the apparent strength.

Markets assigned roughly 62% odds to a September BOJ increase. The IMF's Dan Katz said inflation modestly above target left room for continued normalization. Fiscal questions also remained around Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's growth and defense initiatives and proposed two-year food-tax cut. A calmer auction reduces the immediate spillover to Treasuries; higher local yields can still encourage Japanese savings to stay at home.

The latest Fed disclosure gave a concrete answer on one funding route for yen intervention. FIMA averaged zero in the week through August 5, its eighth unused week, so recent operations were not financed through that facility during the disclosed period. Foreign monetary authorities withdrew about $17 billion from the Fed's foreign reverse-repo pool, leaving $318 billion; the balance had fallen nearly $35 billion in two weeks. Those figures show cash mobilization by official institutions, but do not identify the authority making the withdrawal.

FIMA costs 3.75% overnight or one-week OIS plus 25 basis points, above private repo, and its $60 billion daily counterparty limit is close to one recent Japanese operation's estimated size. Nonuse does not by itself prove Treasury sales: deposits, maturing securities and private funding remain alternatives. The disclosure narrows what is known about intervention financing without identifying the ultimate reserve assets used.

Banxico unanimously held at 6.50% and repeated that rates should remain there at its next meeting. The change was in its inflation forecast: convergence to 3% moved from the second to the fourth quarter of 2027. Services inflation remained 4.36% despite headline slowing to 3.1%. Two-year swaps rose 5 basis points to 6.72%, responding to persistence and guidance rather than a surprise decision.

India continued to move the other way after its 5.25% hold. The one-year swap led declines, the next expected increase shifted from October to December, and markets priced about 50 basis points of tightening over a year rather than roughly 75 before the meeting. The RBI's growth forecast for the year through March 2027 had risen from 6.6% to 6.7%, inflation remained within the 2%–6% band, and the rupee recovered nearly 2% from its low. Investors were giving the bank more time to see whether temporary supply pressure spread into core inflation.

Russia's easing faced less favorable inflation revisions. The Bank of Russia cut 25 basis points to 14% in July while lifting its year-end inflation forecast from 4.5%–5.5% to 6%–7% and lowering 2026 growth from 0.5%–1.5% to 0%–1%. Annual inflation reached 6.11%. Putin's public preference for lower rates and business demands for relief added pressure alongside wartime fiscal needs. The bank retained a 4% inflation target for 2027, leaving more weight on its expectation that current shocks would prove temporary.

## Colombia's pause draws dissent; Argentina extends a reserve backstop

EM dollar debt faced a less favorable common backdrop as oil and US yields rose. The Dollar Index gained 0.26% to 99.95, EMB lost 0.23% and the 15-year-plus dollar sovereign index fell 0.14%. The long sovereign gauge held up better than US long-duration credit. Oil-importing currencies, including the rand and forint, weakened as the Hormuz restrictions emerged, while Ukraine's dollar bonds led country losses.

Colombian central-bank co-director Mauricio Villamizar said the 12% policy rate was insufficient to bring inflation below 4%, the top of the target band, by end-2027. He had favored a 50-basis-point increase in the July 31 vote, which ended 4–3 for a hold. Inflation was forecast near 7% at end-2026 and above 4% in 2027, against a 3% target with a 1-percentage-point tolerance. Fiscal expansion and wages rising faster than productivity were placing more of the adjustment on monetary policy.

The bank also plans to accumulate up to $4 billion through put options after reserve-adequacy measures deteriorated following the loss of access to the IMF Flexible Credit Line. The peso has gained almost 20% this year and rose for a third session, erasing losses associated with the reserve announcement. Villamizar described the program as rebuilding buffers rather than targeting an exchange rate. Dollar purchases nonetheless connect that effort to the currency strength that has helped contain imported inflation.

Argentina obtained a more concrete reserve bridge. Its central bank renewed a roughly $19 billion currency swap with the People's Bank of China for five years, extending the liquidity source beyond the 2027 presidential election. After relying on local dollar borrowing, bank loans and multilateral guarantees rather than accepting external bond yields, the renewal gives it more time to rebuild buffers and meet foreign-currency obligations. It is additional official liquidity, not a completed reopening of bond-market access.

Philippine investors were already demanding more yield for persistent inflation. The ten-year yield rose 52 basis points in July to about 7.25%, and local bonds lost 1.74%, the weakest Southeast Asian performance. July inflation eased for a third month to 6.2%, but remained well above the 3% full-year target. Markets priced a 25-basis-point increase at the August 27 meeting.

Analysts expected ten-year yields between 7.20% and 7.60%, with one forecast reaching 7.60%–7.80%. Demand was expected to improve above 7.50%, where the steep curve provided more compensation for further tightening. The recent inflation slowdown was therefore not enough to remove the local duration risk, particularly with oil and the dollar turning higher again.

## Equity volatility stays low despite the energy reversal

WTI's 3.80% rise to $78.08 and the dollar's 0.26% gain to 99.95 accompanied increases in both Treasury breakevens and real yields. Gold futures also rose 1.72% to $4,318.80. The energy reversal renewed inflation concerns without eliminating demand for protection against policy and geopolitical uncertainty.

Equities were comparatively calm. The S&P 500 fell 0.18% and the Nasdaq 100 lost 0.39%, while semiconductors gained 0.33%. VIX declined 4.17% to 15.15. That was not the pattern of a broad rush out of risk, even as bond investors marked down duration and sought concessions on AI debt.

The primary market supplied the clearest evidence that financing remained available: Alphabet completed its jumbo sale during the Treasury selloff. High-yield funds fell less than investment-grade duration and EM losses were modest. The pressure was most visible in rates and particular transaction terms, not in a general inability to transfer risk.

## Payrolls and the trading after Alphabet's sale

August 7 payroll consensus calls for 80,000 jobs after 57,000, with unemployment unchanged at 4.2%. The report will help separate low new layoffs from the harder re-employment suggested by continuing claims. Hiring breadth, wages and participation matter alongside the headline. Strong hiring with firm wages would give Daly's faster-response scenario and Musalem's inflation concerns more relevance; weaker employment and costs would reduce the urgency of another hike.

Hormuz requires access that works for ships and insurers, not merely an agreement among some of the parties. Excluded flags, attacks or continued insurance friction would preserve Thursday's energy risk. Rising traffic through an accepted route, with lower freight and insurance obstacles, would restore the practical basis for the earlier oil-led bond rally.

Alphabet's secondary trading will test whether its orderbook represented lasting capacity at the new price. Investors can compare the new two- to 40-year curve with February's bonds and subsequent corporate or data-center deals. Stable outstanding paper and new issues clearing near secondary levels would suggest the concession was sufficient. Repeated widening or larger premiums would show that the recurring calendar is still putting pressure on investment-grade and securitized-credit portfolios.
